entities.summary:
Prada, founded in 1913 in Milan by Mario Prada as a leather goods store, is one of the world's most prestigious luxury fashion houses, transformed from a family leather business to a global luxury conglomerate by Miuccia Prada (Mario's granddaughter) and Patrizio Bertelli since 1978. Prada's nylon backpack (1984) — deliberately using industrial material in luxury fashion — was one of the most conceptually influential design decisions in luxury goods history, establishing the brand's intellectual anti-fashion stance.

Mario Prada opened his first shop in the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II in Milan in 1913, supplying Milanese aristocracy with leather handbags, trunks, and accessories. The Savoy royal family appointed Prada as official supplier in 1919. Miuccia Prada, who had studied political science and worked as a mime artist before reluctantly taking over the family business, brought an intellectual rigor to fashion that distinguished Prada from traditional luxury houses.

Miuccia's 1984 nylon backpack decision — making luxury from industrial material used in parachutes and tents — combined luxury pricing with anti-luxury materials in a paradox that became Prada's DNA. Miuccia's collections consistently engage with feminist theory, ugliness as aesthetic strategy, and intellectual references to art history, making Prada the most critically discussed fashion brand globally. The Prada Epicenter stores (OMA/Rem Koolhaas, 2001) redefined the luxury retail experience. Miu Miu (1992) extended Prada to a younger demographic.
